title: Crossing into Sweden and the German officer who knew Greer
summary: A German major recognises him from Chicago; later he turns out to be an intelligence colonel.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Well, anyway, we got out of there and went to Sweden. We had the -- Irving Mills bribed some guys so he had a boat, he took us by boat over there. The guy that took all that transportation and everything, so now we stayed in Sweden for a while, and we had to go to some little town. I don't recall what it was -- I don't recall now, but we had to go over German borders, you know, and you had a set-up -- German thing. So now we're coming through the line and we had to show the passports.

We showed our passports and so now I'm in the line in back of Ivie, so I come to the line and they say, my passport said William Greer, that's my name. Sonny's a nickname, so the guy -- here's the guy with a major's uniform, one of the German officers, so when I get up to the line, he says, "Hello, Sonny, man, what do you know, how you doing". I said, "My name's William." Oh, he say, "Man, go ahead, your name's Sonny." I say, he said, "I saw you in Chicago, at Oriental Theatre."
: He saw you at the Oriental.

Yeah, wait, now get this. Now, he's a major in the German army. He took me aside, he said, 'I saw talking you at the Oriental Theatre,' soft, didn't want them other cats to hear him. I say, 'Yeah, What did we play?' He said, man do you still play 'Ring Dem Bells', and sing 'Mood Indigo'. He named every number we played.

So I look at this cat to be a big major in the German army, sharp, big cat. Oh, he was big. I said to him, I say, 'Man, if you know so much, what you doing in that uniform?' He look all around and he say, 'don't say nothing. He say I tell you when I see you in Chicago.' 'When will you be in Chicago?' I told him about three months from now. He say 'I'll come backstage and see you.'

I forgot all about it. So man, we're playing the Palace Theatre in Chicago, I come offstage and the doorman said, 'Hey, Sonny, there's a Colonel in the United States Army want to see you.' I say, 'Yeah, me.' Yeah. So I went down there and here's this cat. Now, he's a colonel in the -- I say, 'Man, what's going down, what's wrong with you.' He say, 'Well, man, I was in the Intelligence Department. What the hell, I told you I'd see you.'
Me and him went to the juice joint and had a ball.
How did you learn to speak German?
Oh, that's right, you learned to speak German in Long Branch. My teacher in high school. My teacher
Had the orchestra, man. This cat was jiving -- I told the German teacher, I can beat him playing. Remember I toldyou that.
